Summary


The entry level attorney is expected to have a superior academic record from a law school recognized as offering a strong academic program. The entry level Legal Assistant/Attorney assists other Division attorneys by performing research and drafting correspondence and memoranda.
*Admission to a recognized bar must be obtained within 14 months after appointment. Title of Legal Assistant will be used until notification of bar admission.



Duties and Responsibilities


1. Performs legal research in support of more experienced attorneys.  This includes complex merger and acquisition transactions involving consideration of federal and state banking law, securities and antitrust law, corporate and accounting issues, international financial matters, litigation in which the Board is a party or has an interest, and enforcement actions against financial institutions and directors, which require the ability to identify and suggest resolutions to difficult business and legal issues.

2. Prepares draft memoranda and correspondence on matters for which there is clear precedent and matters requiring extensive legal research to identify issues, propose resolutions, and construct alternate arguments.

3. Responds to inquiries (from Board staff, Reserve Bank staff, other regulatory agencies, financial institutions, and the public) relating to the interpretation of banking law and other regulatory matters which are fairly clear-cut.

4. Renders preliminary determinations under the Government in the Sunshine Act.  Applies the requirements of the Act to determinations as to whether Board agenda items should be considered at a Board meeting open (or closed) to the public.

5. Reviews paralegal work responding to Freedom of Information Act requests.

About the Job
The Attorney will work in the Banking Regulation and Policy group (BRPG) of the Board’s Legal Division. Attorneys in BRPG advise the Board of Governors, the General Counsel, and other Federal Reserve staff on a variety of legal and policy issues related to the regulation and supervision of banks, bank holding companies, savings and loan holdings companies, and foreign banks.

Provide legal advice on matters involving the interpretation of financial statutes, regulations, standards, and guidance; proposed financial legislation; bank supervisory issues, including international banking issues; and applications and related matters involving domestic and foreign banking organizations, such as banking applications and expansionary activity proposals, petitions, and requests for legal interpretations.


Requirements for FR-25:
Requires a law degree (JD) from an accredited law school; and admission to a recognized U.S. Bar must be obtained within 14 months of appointment. Membership in good standing with a U.S. Bar is required thereafter, through duration of employment in the Legal Division as an attorney. Title of Legal Assistant will be used until notification of bar admission.

Requirements for FR-26:
Requires a law degree (JD) from an ABA accredited law school; and must be an active member in good standing of the bar of a state, territory of the United States, the District of Columbia, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico prior to and throughout duration of employment as an attorney. Requires a minimum of one year as a practicing attorney in private practice or government agency with relevant legal experience, with developing skills and expertise including laws, regulations and policies that apply to the assigned practice area (e.g., banking law, administrative law, or other practice area).

Requirements for FR-27:
Requires a law degree (JD) from an ABA accredited law school; and must be an active member in good standing of the bar of a state, territory of the United States, the District of Columbia, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico prior to and throughout duration of employment as an attorney. Requires a minimum of two years as a practicing attorney in private practice or government agency with relevant legal experience, with developing skills and expertise including laws, regulations and policies that apply to the assigned practice area (e.g., banking law, administrative law, or other practice area).


Requirements at all levels:
Must demonstrate excellent oral and written communication skills, strong analytic and interpersonal skills (including the ability to interact effectively with management and staff at all levels of the organization), personal initiative, and adaptability in working across legal disciplines. Must also possess excellent attention to detail and strong organizational skills (including ability to handle multiple assignments and organize projects and see through their successful completion with minimal supervision). Requires sound judgment and a high level of discretion as will have access to highly sensitive information. In addition:

  • U.S. citizenship required. 
  • Successful completion of background check required.
